segments.text: It's a scorching summer day, and Gumgumi starts climbing a mountain.
The higher he goes, the closer he gets to the sun.
But the summit turns out to be much colder.
Air is basically transparent, so sunlight passes right through it.
That light warms the ground, and the ground warms the air right above it.
Higher up, lower pressure lets the air expand and cool.
So mountains stay colder even though they're closer to the sun.
